leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - 2010 pride parade discrimination ruling
leads.documents: ECHR fine against Russia for systemic refusal of local governments to issue permits for pride parades; establishes state discrimination against LGBTQ assembly, applicable in Tuva as federal precedent.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as: 'In 2010, the European Court of Human Rights fined Russia for discriminating against the LGBTQ community, after local governments systemically refused to issue permits to pride parades' and 'In 2010, Russia was fined by the European Court of Human Rights, ruling that, as alleged by Alexeyev, Russian cities were discriminating against the gay community'

leads.title: Federal Law on propaganda of non-traditional sexual relationships (2013)
leads.documents: Criminalizes distribution of 'propaganda' promoting 'non-traditional sexual relationships' among minors; basis for censorship, arrests, and documented increase in homophobic hate crimes.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as: 'In 2013, Russia passed a law criminalising the distribution of "propaganda" promoting "non-traditional sexual relationships" among minors' unanimously passed by Russian Duma

leads.title: United Nations Human Rights Council expert panel report - 13 April 2017
leads.documents: Panel of five expert advisors condemning wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya; documents enforcement pattern of detention, torture, extrajudicial killing.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as: 'In a report issued on 13 April 2017, a panel of five expert advisors to the United Nations Human Rights Council condemned the wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya'

leads.title: 2022 expansion of propaganda law
leads.documents: Expands 2013 law to all ages and prohibits distribution of materials that make minors interested in gender transitions; directly targets transgender visibility and information.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as: 'in 2022, the "propaganda" law was expanded to apply to anyone regardless of age group, and to also prohibit the distribution of materials that make minors interested in gender transitions'

leads.title: Federal Law banning gender transition - July 2023 (with 1 July 2023 implementation)
leads.documents: Bans gender-affirming care/surgery and legal gender recognition outright; prohibits trans people changing legal gender; core legal status risk for trans visitors/residents.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as: 'In July 2023, Russia enacted a law banning gender transition which prohibited both gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition outright' and 'The Russian government introduced new laws on 1 July 2023'

leads.title: Federal Law banning adoption by citizens of countries allowing gender transition - 2024
leads.documents: Bans adoption of Russian children by citizens/permanent residents of countries that allow gender transitions; shows state machinery linking gender-transition policy to family law.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as: 'in 2024 passed a law banning the adoption of Russian children by citizens or permanent residents of countries that allow gender transitions'

leads.title: Supreme Court of Russia ruling November 2023 + 22 March 2024 unified extremist list entry
leads.documents: Designates 'the international LGBT public movement' / 'international LGBT social movement and its structural units' as extremist, added to unified list of terrorist and extremist organizations; criminalizes leading, participating, funding, or displaying symbols like rainbow flag.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as: 'In November 2023, the Supreme Court issued a ruling designating "the international LGBT public movement" as an extremist group' and 'On 22 March 2024, the "international LGBT social movement and its structural units" (Russian: Международное общественное движение ЛГБТ и его структурные подразделения) was formally added to the "unified list of terrorist and extremist organizations and persons"'

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - Fedotova and Others v. Russia (2021)
leads.documents: Rules Russia's failure to offer any legal recognition to same-sex relationships violates human rights; documents lack of same-sex unions protection, followed by Russia leaving court in 2022.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as: 'In the 2021 case Fedotova and Others v. Russia, the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg ruled that it was a violation of human rights for Russia not to offer any form of legal recognition to same-sex relationships. However, Russia left the court in 2022'

leads.title: Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) report - December 2018
leads.documents: Confirms claims that persecution of LGBTQ persons in Chechnya took place and was ignored by authorities; institutional verification of forced disappearances, secret abductions, imprisonment, torture in camps.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as: 'A report released in December 2018 by the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) confirmed claims that persecution of LGBTQ persons had taken place and was ignored by authorities'

leads.title: Novaya Gazeta reporting - 1 April 2017 on Chechnya anti-gay purges + Russian LGBT Network follow-up
leads.documents: Initial documentation that since February 2017 over 100 men detained/tortured and at least three extrajudicially killed in 'prophylactic sweep'; follow-up on Dec 2018-Jan 2019 purge with ~40 detained and two killed; documents enforcement risk and evacuation difficulties.
leads.detail: No URL in excerpt; cited as: 'Allegations were initially reported on 1 April 2017 in Novaya Gazeta... which reported that since February 2017 over 100 men had allegedly been detained and tortured and at least three had died' and 'On 11 January 2019, it was reported that another ‘gay purge’ had begun... The Russian LGBT Network believes that around 40 persons were detained and two killed'
